question: Azathioprine is a prodrug of 6mercaptopurine and is used as an immunosuppressant. How is it transformed into 6mercaptopurine ?:

options.opd: By the action of xanthine oxidase.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Azathioprine -> metabolized in the liver -> converted to 6-mercaptopurine -> by xanthine oxidase -> 70% CHAIN: Azathioprine -> undergoes a non-enzymatic conversion -> to 6-mercaptopurine -> through nucleophilic attack of glutathione -> 60% CHAIN: Azathioprine -> activated by amidophosphoribosyl transferase -> converted to 6-mercaptopurine -> by hydrolysis with esterases -> 75% CHAIN: Azathioprine -> metabolized by thiopurine methyltransferase -> transformed into 6-mercaptopurine -> through sulphatase hydrolysis -> 70%
analysis: Azathioprine is metabolized in the body through a process involving the enzyme thiopurine methyltransferase (TPMT) and xanthine oxidase, leading to the formation of 6-mercaptopurine.
